content.title: About
content.content: Canned carrots cooked in vegetable oil are peeled, sliced, blanched and then sealed in a jar with added oil. The product is ready to eat, retaining a bright orange colour, soft texture and a mildly sweet flavour.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canned carrots are often used as an ingredient in salads, side dishes and cold appetizers.
The oil in the jar helps retain moisture and enhances the taste.
Carrots are rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Canning allows storage for up to 2‑3 years at room temperature.
In some countries carrots are canned in olive oil, giving them a Mediterranean aroma.

items.title: Rich source of vitamin A
items.content: Beta‑carotene from carrots is converted into vitamin A, essential for vision, immunity and skin health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Carotenoids and vitamin C protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fibre in carrots promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Provides potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and blood pressure.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: A 100 g serving contains about 80 kcal, making it suitable for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Oil content
items.content: The product contains vegetable oil, so those monitoring fat intake should consider its calories.

items.title: Salt and preservatives
items.content: Some varieties add salt or preservatives; people with hypertension or sensitivities should check the label.

items.title: Carrot allergy
items.content: Rare, but an allergic reaction to carrots is possible.

items.title: Can integrity
items.content: If the lid is damaged or the jar is bulging, the product may be spoiled and pose a food‑borne illness risk.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned carrots can be eaten straight from the jar, added to salads, stews, pasta, omelets, or used as a side dish for meat and fish. They can also be gently warmed in a pan if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated in a sealed container for no more than 5‑7 days. Discard if an off‑odor or discoloration appears.
